questions.question: The value added of a firm is calculated as ________.

options.text: value of production of the firm – value of intermediate goods used by the firm
value of production of the firm + value of capital goods used by the firm
value of production of the firm / value of intermediate goods used by the firm
value of production of the firm + value of intermediate goods used by the firm

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**value of production of the firm – value of intermediate goods used by the firm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Value Added

 
 
• Value-added describes the value that a company adds to a raw material or intermediate good during the production process.
 
• The difference between the value of output and the value of intermediate products is used to calculate the national income using the value-added method.
 
 

 Value Added = Value of Output – Intermediate

 
• Value Added Method

 
 
• In a circular flow, national income is calculated using the value-added method at various phases of the production process. In the production process, it indicates the value added for each unit produced.
 
• Every business adds value to the goods it purchases as an intermediary good from other firms.
 
• The value of national income is the sum total of value added by all organisations.
 
• The following steps are used to calculate national income using the value-added method:
 
 
• Step 1
 
• The first step is to identify and classify all value of producing enterprises in primary, secondary, and tertiary sectors.
 
• Step 2
 
• Next, the Gross Domestic Product at Market Prices (GDPMP) is calculated.
 
• Determine the Gross Value Added at Market Price (GVAMP) of each sector for the purpose of calculating the GDPMP; i.e. ∑GVAMP = GDPMP
 
• Step 3
 
• Next, determine domestic income (NDPFC).
 
• Value of depreciation and net indirect tax are deducted from the gross domestic product at market price (GDPMP) to calculate domestic income; NDPFC = GDPMP – Depreciation – Net Indirect Taxes
 
• Step 4
 
• To determine national income (NNPFC), the final step is to calculate Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA).
 
• The NFIA is added along with the country's domestic income; National Income or NNPFC = Domestic Income or NDPFC + NFIA

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct regarding mixtures?

options.text: Colloids are heterogeneous mixtures in which the particle size is large.
The major component of a solution is called the solvent.
The minor component of a solution is called the solute.
A solution is a homogeneous mixture of two or more substances

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Colloids are heterogeneous mixtures in which the particle size is large **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A mixture is a combination of two or more substances that are not chemically bonded to each other.
 
• Mixtures can be classified into two types: homogeneous and heterogeneous.
 
• Homogeneous mixtures have a uniform composition throughout, whereas heterogeneous mixtures have a non-uniform composition.
 
• The components of a mixture can be separated by physical methods such as filtration, distillation, chromatography, etc.
 
• Filtration is used to separate a solid from a liquid or a gas.
 
• Distillation is used to separate a mixture of two or more liquids with different boiling points.
 
• **Colloids**, also known as colloidal solutions or colloidal systems, are mixtures in which microscopically dispersed insoluble particles of one substance are suspended in another substance. 
 
• The size of the suspended particles in a colloid can range from 1 to 1000 nanometres (10-9 meters) which is **very small**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Solution **

 
• A solution is a homogeneous mixture of two or more substances, where one substance is called the solute and the other is called the solvent.
 
• The solute is the substance that is dissolved in the solvent, whereas the solvent is the substance in which the solute is dissolved.
 
• Solutions can be classified as solid, liquid, or gaseous, depending on the physical state of the solvent.
 
• The concentration of a solution is the amount of solute present in a given amount of solvent or solution.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is correct regarding air pressure?

options.text: High pressure is associated with cloudy skies and wet weather.
Low pressure is associated with clear and sunny skies.
The air always moves from high pressure areas to low pressure areas.
The air pressure is lowest at sea level and increases with height.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The air always moves from high pressure areas to low pressure areas.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] 

**__Key Points__**

 
• ​The **air always moves from high-pressure areas to low-pressure areas.**
 
• This i**s because air always moves along pressure gradients, from areas of high pressure to areas of low pressure, in an attempt to equalize the pressure.**
 
• This movement of air is what we experience as wind.

***Hence statement 3 is correct.***

 
• **High pressure** is generally associated with** clear skies and calm weather, not cloudy and wet weather.**
 
• This is** because high pressure involves air sinking toward the surface of the earth,** which** inhibits cloud formation.**

*Hence statement 1 is incorrect.*

 
• Conversely, l**ow pressure is often associated with cloudy skies and wet weather, not clear and sunny skies.**
 
• Low pressure involves **air rising from the earth's surface, which can lead to cloud formation and precipitation.**

*Hence statement 2 is incorrect.*

 
• The air pressure is **highest at sea level and decreases with height.**
 
• This is due to the** weight of the air above compressing the air at lower levels (like sea level), making it denser and therefore exerting more pressure.**
 
• As you go higher, **there's less air above you, so the pressure decreases.**
 
• **For this reason, it is difficult to breathe in the hilly areas and mountains.**

*Hence statement 4 is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/afedd0fb0448f6756d09c3e269e2da237898fdd92c1b7c3d8ff6926800c6dd39.png]

questions.question: Carnatic music is confined to ______.

options.text: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal and Haryana
Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Kerala

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Kerala**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Carnatic Music__

 __
 
• **Carnatic music is one of the forms of Indian classical music.**
 
• It is confined to southern India, the states of** Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamilnadu, and Kerala** while the **classical music of the rest of the country is under the name of Hindustani.**
 
• The main emphasis in **Carnatic music is on the vocals.**
 
• The music is created in the **traditional octave form and the music is Kriti based** and focuses more on the** Sahithya or the lyric quality of the musical piece.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ​Trinity of Carnatic Music__

 
 
• The Three Jewels of Carnatic music referred to trio composers – being **Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, and Syama Sastri also known as the Trinity of Carnatic music.**
 
• All three of the Trinities lived and composed music in **Thanjavur, Tamilnadu.**
 
• Thanjavur has been the capital of **Carnatic Music, not only because the Trinities lived there but also because the place has nurtured Carnatic music for a long time.**
 
• The** Kings from Thanjavur – the Cholas, Nayaks, and the Marathas –** have consistently supported **Carnatic music and the artists, and contributed to its current-day greatness and preservation. **
 
• Muthuswami Dikshitar was the youngest of the trinities.

questions.question: Which among the following statements is incorrect?

options.text: Industrial Securities Market is also known as gilt-edged market.
The secondary market is the market for the sale and purchase of previously issued securities.
RBI plays a dominant role in the gilt-edged market through its ‘Open Market Operations’.
The primary market is also known as new issue market.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Option 1.**__** **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **No, the Industrial Securities Market** is not commonly known as the** gilt-edged market.**
 
• **The gilt-edged market, also known as the gilt market,** refers to the market for government bonds in the **United Kingdom.** These bonds are considered to be low-risk investments because they are backed by the UK government and are therefore seen as** "gilt-edged" investments.**
 
• On the other hand, the Industrial Securities Market refers to the market where industrial securities are traded. These securities include stocks, shares, and other investment products issued by companies in the industrial sector. This market is also commonly known as the stock market or the equity market.
 
• While both the gilt-edged market and the industrial securities market are important parts of the financial system, they are distinct markets with different investment products and characteristics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The secondary market is a financial market **where investors buy and sell securities that have already been issued by companies or other entities. In contrast to **the primary market, where securities are issued for the first time, the secondary market involves the trading of existing securities between investors.**

 
 
• The secondary market includes exchanges such as **the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) and the NASDAQ, as well as over-the-counter (OTC) markets where securities** are traded directly between buyers and sellers without a centralized exchange. In the secondary market, the price of a security is determined by supply and demand, and fluctuations in market conditions can affect the price of securities traded on the market.
 
 
 
• ** The Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** plays a dominant role in the **gilt-edged market through its open market operations (OMOs)**.
 
 
• In the gilt-edged market, government securities (G-secs) are traded, and these securities are issued by the government to raise funds.
 
• The **RBI **is responsible for managing the demand and supply of G-secs in the market. One of the primary tools that the RBI uses to manage the demand and supply of **G-secs is through OMOs**.**OMOs are the buying and selling of government securities in the open market by the RBI.** 
 
• When th**e RBI wants to inject liquidity into the market**, it buys G-secs from the market, and when it wants to absorb liquidity from the market, it sells G-secs in the market. This helps in regulating the** money supply in the economy and controlling inflation.**
 
 
 
• **The primary market**, also known as the **new issue market,** is where **new securities are issued and sold for the first time to investors**.
 
 
• Companies, governments, and other organizations raise capital in the primary market by selling securities, such as stocks or bonds, to investors. The primary market is distinct from the secondary market, where securities that have already been issued are bought and sold between investors.

questions.question: Tropic of Cancer (23°30′ N) passes through ______ state of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Option 3.**__** **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• ** The Tropic of Cancer (23°30′ N)** passes through 8 states of India, namely **Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, and Mizoram.**
 
• **The Tropic of Cancer is an imaginary line of latitude that circles the Earth at approximately 23.5 degrees north of the equator**. It is one of the five major circles of latitude that mark maps of the Earth.
 
• 
 
**The Tropic of Cancer passes through or near several countries including Mexico, the Bahamas, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, India, and China.** It is also an important point for understanding the Earth's climate, as it marks the northern boundary of the tropics and the point where the Sun appears directly overhead on the summer solstice in the northern hemisphere.

 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Punjab is a state located in the northern region of India.**

• The capital city of Punjab is Chandigarh, which is a union territory and also serves as the capital of the neighboring state of Haryana.
 
 
 
• 
 
**Maharashtra is a state located in the western region of India. **

 
 
• 
 
It is the **second-most populous state** in** India** and has **Mumbai** as its capital city, which is also known as the financial capital of India.** The state covers an area of 307,713 square kilometers and has a population of over 123 million people.**

 
 
• 
 
**Maharashtra is bordered by the Arabian Sea to the west, Gujarat to the northwest, Madhya Pradesh to the northeast, Chhattisgarh to the east, Telangana to the southeast, Karnataka to the south, and Goa to the southwest.**

 
 
• 
 
The state is known for its rich history, diverse culture, and varied landscapes, including the Western Ghats mountain range, the Deccan Plateau, and the coastal region. Maharashtra is also home to several major industries, including the entertainment industry centered in Mumbai, the financial industry, and the manufacturing industry.

 
 
 
 
• **Kerala is a state located in the southwestern region of India.**
 
 
• 
 
It is bordered by the **Arabian Sea to the west, Karnataka to the north, and Tamil Nadu to the east**. *Thiruvananthapuram* is the capital city of **Kerala.**

 
 
• 
 
**Kerala** is known for its** natural beauty, including its palm-lined beaches, serene backwaters, lush green hills, and wildlife reserves**. The state is also famous for its cuisine, which features a variety of vegetarian and non-vegetarian dishes that are rich in spices and flavors.

 
 
• 
 
**Kerala is a highly literate state with a strong focus on education, healthcare, and social welfare**. The state has a diverse population and a rich cultural heritage that is reflected in its art, music, and dance forms.

questions.question: Which among the following films received the Filmfare award for the Best Film popular choice in 2022?

__
 
• The Filmfare Awards are one of the most prestigious film awards in India.

questions.question: What is the average height of troposphere?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** The troposphere is the lowest layer of the Earth's atmosphere**, extending from the surface up to an average altitude of about **7 to 12 kilometers (4.3 to 7.5 miles).**
 
• The height of the troposphere varies depending on the location, season, and weather conditions. However, the average height of the troposphere is about **11 kilometers (6.8 miles) above sea level**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Earth's atmosphere** can be divided into **five primary layers **based on **their temperature and altitude**:

 
 
• **Troposphere**: This is the lowest layer of the Earth's atmosphere, extending from the surface up to an average altitude of 12 kilometers (7.5 miles) at the equator. The majority of Earth's weather occurs in this layer, and it is where most of the Earth's greenhouse gases are concentrated.
 
• **Stratosphere**: This layer lies above the troposphere, extending from about 12 to 50 kilometers (7.5 to 31 miles) in altitude. The ozone layer is located in this layer, which absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation from the sun.
 
• Mesosphere: Above the stratosphere, the mesosphere extends from about 50 to 85 kilometers (31 to 53 miles) in altitude. This layer is known for its extremely low temperatures, as low as -100°C (-148°F) at the top.
 
• **Thermosphere**: This layer extends from about 85 kilometers (53 miles) to the edge of space, around 600 kilometers (372 miles) above the Earth's surface. The temperature increases with altitude in this layer, reaching up to 2,000°C (3,632°F) due to the absorption of solar radiation.
 
• **Exosphere:** The outermost layer of Earth's atmosphere, the exosphere, begins at an altitude of about 600 kilometers (372 miles) and extends into space. This layer is where the Earth's atmosphere gradually thins out and merges with the vacuum of space.

questions.question: In which year Mahatma Gandhi organised a satyagraha in the Kheda district of Gujarat in the support of peasants?

__
 
• Mahatma Gandhi organized a Satyagraha in the **Kheda district of Gujarat in the year 1918.**
 
• **The Satyagraha** was a **non-violent resistance movement in support of the peasants** who were facing immense difficulties due to the oppressive policies of the British government, particularly the high taxes they imposed on the farmers.
 
• **The Satyagraha **was successful in achieving its objectives, and it helped establish** Mahatma Gandhi's leadership in the Indian independence movement.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Mahatma Gandhi (Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi) was born on October 2, 1869.
 
• He was an Indian lawyer, politician, social activist, and writer.
 
• He became the leader of the nationalist movement against the British rule of India.
 
• He was known as the Father of the Nation.
 
• Gandhi is internationally esteemed for his doctrine of nonviolent protest (Satyagraha) to achieve political and social progress.
 
• He died January 30, 1948, in Delhi, and the day is celebrated as Shaheed Diwas or Martyrs' Day.
 
• His autobiography is titled My Experiments with Truth.
 
• Important movements led by Mahatma Gandhi:
 
 
• ​Champaran Movement (1917)
 
• Kheda Movement (1918)
 
• Khilafat Movement (1919)
 
• Non-Cooperation Movement (1920)
 
• Civil Disobedience Movement: Dandi March (1930)
 
• Quit India Movement (1942)

questions.question: A ______ is an electronic device that receives a weak signal and regenerates it.
questions.solution:

• A **repeater **is a device that receives a **signal**, amplifies it, and then **re-transmits it to extend its range or reach.**
 
• **Repeaters** are commonly used in** telecommunications** and** broadcasting** to **increase the coverage area of signals**, particularly in **areas with obstacles** or** weak signal strength.**
 
• **Repeaters **can also be used in **networking to extend the range** of a **wireless network or to improve signal quality.**
 
• Additionally, in firearms, a **"repeater"** can refer to a **type of gun **that can **quickly fire multiple rounds** without needing to** reload after each shot.**

questions.question: The plants of which of the following plant kingdoms are known as algae?
questions.solution:
The correct option is **Thallophyta**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points:__**__Concept:__

__
 
• Based on whether plants have a well-differentiated body and the presence or absence of specialized tissues for transport, and the ability to bear seeds Kingdom Plantae (Plant Kingdom) is can be classified into different divisions.
 
• Thallophyta
 
 
• The plant body is not differentiated from roots, stems, and leaves.
 
• They are commonly called algae.
 
 
 
• Bryophyta
 
 
• These are small terrestrial plants.
 
• They show differentiation in the body design, with stem, leaf-like structures, and root-like structures.
 
 
 
• Pteridophyta
 
 
• The plant body is differentiated into roots, stems, and leaves, apart from having a specialized tissue for conduction.
 
 
 
• Gymnosperms
 
 
• Gymnosperms are plants with naked seeds.
 
 
 
• Angiosperms
 
 
• Angiosperms are seed-bearing plants. Seeds develop inside tissues that get modified to form the fruit of the plant. 
 
 

Explanation:__

 
• All the plants that lack a well-differentiated body structure belong to the subgroup Thallophyta.
 
• Thallophytes are commonly known as algae.
 
• The majority of them are aquatic. 
 
• It includes the primitive form of plant life.
 
• They do not have vascular tissues which help in the transportation of water and minerals, hence, they are usually found in moist places.
 
• Thallophyta is further divided into - Algae and Fungi.
 
• Chara, Lichen, and Spirogyra are examples of Thallophyta.
